nødvendigvis.explanation: "Nødvendigvis" means "necessarily". It comes from "nødvendig" (necessary). To say something is not always true, put "ikke" (not) before it: "Han er ikke nødvendigvis rig" (He is not necessarily rich).

nøgen.explanation: "Nøgen" means "naked". For trees, it also means "bare": "nøgne træer" (bare trees).

nøgtern.explanation: "Nøgtern" means "matter-of-fact". A second meaning is "sober", as in plain and without drama: "nøgterne tal" (sober figures). To say someone has not been drinking, use "ædru" (sober): "Han er ædru" (He is sober).

nøjagtig.explanation: "Nøjagtig" means "exact". A second meaning is "accurate", as in correct in every detail: "Vi har brug for nøjagtige oplysninger" (We need accurate information).

nøjagtigt.explanation: "Nøjagtigt" means "exactly". It comes from "nøjagtig" (exact). To say a number is not exact, use "omtrent" (about): "Der kom omtrent tre hundrede mennesker" (About three hundred people came).

nøje.explanation: "Nøje" means "closely". To tell someone to read with full attention, say: "Læs kontrakten nøje" (Read the contract closely). To say something is not important, use it with "ikke så" (not so): "Det er ikke så nøje" (It does not matter that much).

at observere.explanation: "At observere" means "to observe". To say you watch animals in nature, say: "at observere fuglene" (to observe the birds).

at offentliggøre.explanation: "At offentliggøre" means "to publish / make public". It is built from "offentlig" (public) and "at gøre" (to make). To say an official body makes something known, say: "Regeringen offentliggør planen" (The government makes the plan public).

at ofre.explanation: "At ofre" means "to sacrifice". To say you give up something valuable for others, say: "Hun ofrer sin weekend" (She gives up her weekend). To say someone makes an offering to a god, say: "at ofre til guderne" (to make an offering to the gods).

at omdanne.explanation: "At omdanne" means "to transform". To say what something becomes, add "til" (into): "De omdanner fabrikken til boliger" (They transform the factory into homes).

at omfatte.explanation: "At omfatte" means "to include". It is built from "om" (around) and "at fatte" (to grasp). To say what a price covers, say: "Prisen omfatter morgenmad" (The price includes breakfast).

at omformulere.explanation: "At omformulere" means "to rephrase". The "om" at the start works like "re-" in "at omskrive" (to rewrite). When someone did not understand you, ask: "Kan du omformulere det?" (Can you rephrase that?)

at omgive.explanation: "At omgive" means "to surround". To say what a place is surrounded by, use "omgivet af" (surrounded by): "Huset er omgivet af skov" (The house is surrounded by forest).

at omgå.explanation: "At omgå" means "to bypass / get around". To say you get around a difficulty, say: "Vi omgår problemet" (We get around the problem). Do not mix it up with "at omgås", which means "to socialize": "Jeg omgås mine kolleger" (I socialize with my colleagues).

at omgås.explanation: "At omgås" means "to associate with / socialize". To say who you spend time with, say: "Jeg omgås mest folk fra arbejdet" (I mostly spend time with people from work). Do not mix it up with "at omgå", which means "to bypass": "Lastbilen omgår byen" (The truck goes around the town).

at omringe.explanation: "At omringe" means "to surround". It is built from "om" (around) and "ring" (ring). To say a crowd closes in on something, say: "Folk omringede scenen" (People surrounded the stage).

at omstille sig.explanation: "At omstille sig" means "to adapt". It needs "sig" (yourself), which changes with the person: "jeg omstiller mig" (I adapt) and "de omstiller sig" (they adapt). To say what you adapt to, add "til" (to): "Vi må omstille os til nye regler" (We have to adapt to new rules).

at omstrukturere.explanation: "At omstrukturere" means "to restructure". The "om" at the start works like "re-" in "at omskrive" (to rewrite). To say a city changes how its schools are organized, say: "Kommunen omstrukturerer sine skoler" (The city is restructuring its schools).

at omtale.explanation: "At omtale" means "to mention / refer to". To say you mention a topic, say: "Han omtalte aldrig ulykken" (He never mentioned the accident). To say how someone is described, add "som" (as): "Hun omtales som byens bedste kok" (She is referred to as the best cook in town).

at opbevare.explanation: "At opbevare" means "to store". On a food label, the instruction to store something in a cool place reads: "Opbevares køligt" (Store in a cool place).

at opbygge.explanation: "At opbygge" means "to build up". It is built from "op" (up) and "at bygge" (to build). To say you grow trust slowly, say: "Vi opbygger tillid" (We build up trust). For a house, use "at bygge" instead: "Vi bygger et hus" (We are building a house).

at opdage.explanation: "At opdage" means "to discover". To say you notice a thing, say: "Jeg opdagede en fejl" (I noticed a mistake). To say you find out that something happened, add "at" (that): "Hun opdagede, at tasken var væk" (She discovered that the bag was gone).

at opdatere.explanation: "At opdatere" means "to update". To remind someone to keep a program current, say: "Husk at opdatere appen" (Remember to update the app).

at opdele.explanation: "At opdele" means "to divide". To say you split something into parts, add "i" (into): "Læreren opdeler klassen i fire hold" (The teacher splits the class into four teams). Do not mix it up with "at dele", which means "to share": "Jeg deler kagen med dig" (I share the cake with you).

at opdrage.explanation: "At opdrage" means "to raise (a child)". To say who raises the children, say: "Hun opdrager sine børn alene" (She raises her children alone).
